blocks.text: During the hot, dry summer months, solar power plants operate at high potential, soaking up intense sunlight just as air conditioners push grid demand to record levels. Months later, as monsoon rains fill hydro reservoirs during the wet season, hydroelectric plants step up output while solar power generation ebbs under dense cloud cover. Less obvious, however, is the seasonal behavior of wind power. In a year, the trajectory of grid demand and wind capacity factor present a remarkably inverse relationship.
